posts.currentEventsCheck: Sep 1 2026 sweep triggered an override: FedWatch hike odds swung 40% -> 57% -> 66-68% in a week, 10-yr Treasury at a 19-20 month high, Fed governor publicly floating a hike ahead of the Sep 15-16 FOMC. posts.mathVerified: Payment math recomputed on a 340k 30-yr loan (20% down on the 425k FL median): 6.75% = 2,205.23/mo, 7.00% = 2,262.03/mo, delta 56.79/mo and 682/yr. Quoted as 'about 57 dollars a month'.
posts.engineFix: Fixed a real bug in scripts/civilian-blog-factory.mjs: the llms.txt section-replace built its RegExp from the unescaped literal '## Blog Posts (auto-maintained)', so the parentheses compiled as a capture group and the pattern never matched. llms.txt had been frozen at the first post since Aug 24. Escaped the source and used a function replacer; all 4 posts now listed.

posts.currentEventsCheck: Sep 3 2026 sweep triggered an override: the APCIA/Moore-Lynch actuarial report landed THAT DAY quantifying Florida insurance relief for the first time, and the NFIP authorization lapse date (Sep 30) is 27 days out. Insurance is the top cost question for Gulf Coast civilian buyers and leads our Copilot citations, so this beat the evergreen queue head. Rates were checked (30-yr ~6.72-6.74% Sep 2, up on Middle East escalation) but the Sep 1 post already covered rates; no hurricane threat in the Gulf.
posts.sourcingNotes: NAR FAQ page (last updated Feb 4 2026) carries a stale internal line saying the NFIP expires Dec 11 2026 while its own URL and every other source say Sep 30 2026. FEMA's official reauthorization page was treated as authoritative and the post cites FEMA for the date. Citizens county-level figures (Escambia +0.2%, Santa Rosa +5.5%, avg premiums 3,376 / 3,871) came from the DECEMBER 2025 recommended filing and conflict with the approved March 2026 statewide -8.8%; deliberately NOT published, the county point is made qualitatively instead. My Safe Florida Home eligibility numbers were only available from aggregators (mysafeflhome.com returned 403), so the post sends readers to the official site rather than stating a perishable rule.
